title: Later leaders of the Excelsior Band and how it plays now
summary: After Pope quit, Charlie Lipscomb and then Eddie Langston led the band; today it has about 14, with saxophones, and plays arrangements.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yes. So, as I'm saying now, at the present time, Mr. Eddie Langston, he has the band. I said, he'll get together, you know. Yeah. Yeah, for the carnival. But after I'd given it up, there was a Charlie Lifstein that played with me. He'd taken the band over. Well, it's short-lived, you know. Didn't have it very long. And after he died, this Langston's taking it over.

So there were breaks in the band's history when the band was not playing? How's that? Yes. And then somebody else reformed the band? Is that right? Yes, that's right. Yes, sir. What do you think of the way they play now? Well, I like it very much. What sort of...
Do they change different type of music now to the old stuff? Well, no.
They play the regular same music, you know. They do. How many are in the band today? Oh, I think they must have about the same amount, around 14.
14. Yeah, about 14. But with saxophones now, and taradets too. Yeah, they use taradets, saxophones. Do they use E-flat taradets or ordinary B-flats? No, all B-flats.
Do they have more than one? They have more than one? They might have one too.
Do they play from music most of the time or just head arrangements?
No, they have arrangements. Yes, yes. I want to play a tradition.
But no more funeral marches, just quick time now.
